user_question: What are the latest applications of AI agents in healthcare?
short_answer: AI agents in healthcare are increasingly utilized for diagnostic support, workflow and operational automation, multi-departmental clinical diagnostics, and patient interaction. However, current research relies heavily on simulated environments and laboratory studies rather than real-world clinical deployments.

key_findings.finding: AI systems in healthcare are categorized into conversational agents, workflow/automation assistants, and multimodal decision support agents, utilizing external tool use (such as retrieval-augmented generation) and iterative self-correction mechanisms.

Recent frameworks like coordinated multi-agent systems in healthcare (MASH) and agent hospitals aim to optimize clinical and operational workflows, though evaluations remain predominantly simulated or laboratory-based with limited real-world clinical pilots.

sources.title: AI agent in healthcare: applications, evaluations, and future directions | npj Artificial Intelligence
sources.summary: Discusses AI agent applications in healthcare including agent hospitals, multi-specialist consultations, and coordinated multi-agent systems, while noting risks like hallucination and limited generalizability.

sources.title: Artificial intelligence agents in healthcare research: A scoping review | PLOS One
sources.summary: A scoping review analyzing 43 studies on healthcare AI agents, categorizing them into conversational, workflow/automation, and multimodal decision support systems, and highlighting a heavy reliance on simulated evaluations.

limitations_or_assumptions: The available literature heavily favors simulated evaluations and laboratory studies over real-world clinical trials.
Clinical outcomes and safety endpoints are rarely addressed in the current body of research.
Some research steps failed; the collected evidence may be incomplete.
suggested_next_steps: Prioritize conducting rigorous clinical trials to assess the long-term clinical efficacy and safety of AI agents.
Develop standardized governance frameworks and evaluation metrics for real-world healthcare deployments.
